title: Poetry and Literary Terms (KS4 English Literature)
subject: English Literature
strapline: The vocabulary you need to analyse poems and prose.
facts: Rhythm is the beat of a poem; metre is its regular pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables.
A rhyme scheme is the pattern of end-rhymes, labelled with letters (ABAB, AABB).
Enjambment is when a sentence runs over the line break without punctuation.
A caesura is a deliberate pause in the middle of a line.
Imagery is descriptive language that appeals to the senses.
Tone is the writer’s attitude; mood is the atmosphere created for the reader.
A stanza is a "verse" — a group of lines separated from others.

quick_quiz.q: What is a sentence running over a line break called?
What do we call the pattern of end-rhymes?
What is a group of lines in a poem called?

teacher_tips: Read poems aloud so rhythm, caesura and enjambment are heard, not just labelled.
Link every technique to meaning — form should serve interpretation.
Build a personal glossary students annotate with their own examples.
